basis: Inherited phosphate disorder causing defective skeletal mineralization; renal phosphate wasting does not establish renal damage; hearing-loss frequency unknown.
Complement deficiency; discoid lesions 4/4, oral ulcers 1/1, arthritis 1/3. Bronchiectasis is a separately diagnosed infectious sequela; arthralgia alone does not qualify.
Infectious abscess directly involves the cornea.
Vitelliform macular dystrophy is a retinal disorder, including when visual impairment is initially absent.
Defining metaphyseal and epiphyseal skeletal dysplasia; psychomotor delay and alopecia occur in some reports without established frequency.
Structural cervical vertebral abnormality; no evidence of associated spinal cord or nerve damage.
Intellectual disability, hyperkinetic movement and ataxia define it; muscular dystrophy/myopathy and cataracts each occur in 30–79%.
Developmental brain disorder; ventricular septal defect and eczematoid dermatitis each reported in 1/2 patients. Frequencies come from a very small cohort.
Intellectual disability and cleft palate are defining features; palate belongs to the oral gastrointestinal axis.
Myopathy 8/8 with neuropathy/encephalopathy; sensorineural hearing loss 3/3 and hepatic failure 1/1. Cataract 1/1 omitted by cap; small reported denominators.
Severe intellectual disability and developmental delay in 5/5, with microcephaly and sometimes spasticity; feeding difficulty does not establish gut damage.
Inherited cerebellar dysfunction; immune, blood and other manifestations of particular subtypes are not general features of this umbrella.
Skeletal muscle calcium-pump dysfunction causes exercise-induced stiffness and cramps; no established primary nerve or systemic metabolic disorder.
Congenital neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis is a lysosomal metabolic disease with severe congenital neurodegeneration; common ocular damage is not established for this form.
Keloid scarring, restricted joint mobility and increased optic cup-to-disc ratio form the named diagnostic phenotype.
Inherited myopia is an ocular refractive and growth disorder.
Pigmentary, ocular and brain anomalies define the syndrome; acral skeletal anomalies are also part of its defining diagnostic phenotype.
Localized excessive hair growth affects skin appendages; its location on the ear does not establish hearing or vestibular disease.
Benign peripheral nerve sheath tumour involving multiple nerve fascicles or trunks; skin involvement is not universal.
Cardiac and skeletal/sternal abnormalities define Noonan syndrome; ptosis 20/23 and intellectual disability 8/23 support ocular and neurologic involvement.
Folate transport defect causes immunodeficiency and megaloblastic cytopenias; developmental delay 3/4, delayed myelination 2/2. Oral ulcers 4/4 and skin ulcers 2/4 omitted by cap.
Umbrella for hereditary ear and upper-airway disease; subtype-specific anosmia, lacrimal obstruction and other anomalies do not establish group-wide involvement.
Respiratory-chain metabolic defect; developmental delay 2/2, cerebral atrophy 1/2 and muscle atrophy 1/2. Respiratory failure alone does not establish direct lung damage.
Intellectual disability and distal skeletal anomalies define the syndrome; joint hypermobility 8/18 supports skeletal involvement. Hearing impairment 4/19 is below threshold.
Developmental language disorder affecting expressive language, phonological memory and nonword repetition.
